items.title: Cloud request signing (Content-MD5 + X-Authorization HMAC-SHA1)
items.facts: Content-MD5 = base64(MD5(body)); empty body is sent AND hashed as '{}'. X-Authorization = 'Timestamp=9999999999, Nonce=<uuid4 lowercase>, AccessKey=<AK>, Signature=<hex lower HMAC-SHA1(SecretKey, md5+LF+9999999999+LF+nonce+LF+path)>'. path = encoded URL path only, incl. any regional path prefix, NO query, NO host. Timestamp is a constant. AK/SK are app constants (already in baseline tapo_cloud.dart). Body bytes = compact JSON UTF-8, no ASCII escaping; hash the exact bytes sent. IoT (services-sync, /v2/things) calls are NOT signed.

items.title: TLS trust for the TP-Link cloud (two private roots)
items.facts: Cloud hosts use certs from 'tp-link-CA' (RSA, legacy) and 'TP-Link Cloud Root CA' (EC P-256) that are not in default stores. Verify against system store PLUS these two PEMs. Baseline already has buildContext(tpLinkRootsPem); confirm the asset contains BOTH roots (the EC root dated 2025 may be missing). Never disable verification for cloud hosts.

items.title: Common query parameters on signed account calls
items.facts: Every signed POST carries query: appName=TP-Link_Tapo_Android, appVer, netType=wifi, termID=<terminalUUID>, ospf='Android <rel>', brand=TPLINK, locale (xx_YY, default en_US), then token=<token> when the call needs it. Query is NOT part of the signature. Content-Type 'application/json;charset=UTF-8', Accept json. Baseline sends only token (and omits the common params): add them.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: query carries common params in order

items.title: Account API reply envelope and error mapping
items.facts: Reply = {errorCode:int, msg, result:{...}}. Effective code = envelope errorCode, else int(result.errorCode) (string in result). Non-JSON body -> malformed error. HTTP>=400 with code 0 -> HTTP error. Known codes: -20212 region redirect (result.appServerUrlV2), -20651 token expired, -20652 token mismatch, -20675 logged in elsewhere, -20677 MFA required (result.MFAProcessId + supportedMFATypes), -20601/-20615 wrong credentials (result.remainAttempts), -20661 locked (result.lockedMinutes), -20600 no account, -20602 not activated, -20676 bad MFA code, -23003 app too old. Response cap 16 MiB; timeout 15 s (login) .
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: error code from envelope or result
test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: locked and remain attempts messages

items.title: Cloud sign-in with regional URL discovery
items.facts: 1) POST {https://n-wap.i.tplinkcloud.com}/api/v2/account/getAccountStatusAndUrl {appType, cloudUserName} -> result.appServerUrlV2 (regional base, strip trailing /; fall back to bootstrap). 2) POST {regional}/api/v2/account/login body {appType, appVersion, cloudUserName, cloudPassword, platform:'Android 14', refreshTokenNeeded:false, terminalUUID, terminalName, terminalMeta:'1'}. 3) On -20212 with a DIFFERENT appServerUrlV2 in result: log in once more there. Token in result.token (required). Keep region URL; account fields email/nickname/accountId. Baseline uses bootstrap n-wap-gw.tplinkcloud.com, key appServerUrl (not ...V2) and skips getAccountStatusAndUrl: align to Windows.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: login follows region redirect once
test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: login without token is malformed

items.title: MFA challenge, code request and completion
items.facts: Login error -20677 gives result.MFAProcessId and supportedMFATypes (1 push, 2 email, 3 TOTP, 4 SMS). Send code: POST {region}/api/v2/account/getPushVC4TerminalMFA | getEmailVC4TerminalMFA | getSmsVC4TerminalMFA body {appType, cloudUserName, cloudPassword, terminalUUID[, locale for email/SMS]}; TOTP sends nothing. Complete: POST /api/v2/account/checkMFACodeAndLogin {appType, cloudUserName, code, MFAProcessId, MFAType:int, terminalBindEnabled:true} (trusts the terminal) -> same result as login. Pending state (email, password, region, processId, types) lives in memory only; cleared on success.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: totp type sends no request

items.title: Silent re-login on token expiry
items.facts: On -20651 (expired) -> captchaLogin (/api/v2/account/captchaLogin, same body as login) with the stored password, ONCE then retry. On -20652 / -20675 -> one full /login. Persistent rejection after one re-login raises. Needs the password in memory (Windows keeps it in DPAPI vault when 'keep me signed in'). Baseline stores only the token and has no refresh path: decide password storage (see decisions).
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: expired token relogs in once
test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: second rejection is not retried

items.title: Device list v2 (paged) and camera filtering
items.facts: POST {region}/api/v2/common/getDeviceListByPage?token=.. body {deviceTypeList:['SMART.IPCAMERA','SMART.TAPODOORBELL','SMART.TAPOHUB'], index, limit:20}; index += 20 until empty page or index >= result.totalNum (cap 500 pages). Keep only deviceType in {SMART.IPCAMERA, SMART.TAPODOORBELL} with non-empty deviceId; dedupe by deviceId. Fields: deviceId, deviceMac (normalise to AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF), deviceModel|deviceName, alias, deviceType, status, fwVer, deviceHwVer, role (0 owner, non-zero shared). v2 'status' is NOT a reliable online flag (0 for streaming cameras).
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: device list pages and filters doorbell

items.title: Service URL discovery (getAppServiceUrl)
items.facts: Signed POST {region}/api/v2/common/getAppServiceUrl?token=.. body {serviceIds:[...]} -> result.serviceUrls {id: url}; drop non-string/empty values, strip trailing /. IoT app server id is 'nbu.iot-app-server.app-v2' (baseline asks 'nbu.iot-app-server.app': switch to -v2). Reject URL whose scheme is not http(s) or that is http while the account API is https (refuse insecure IoT URL). Cache per session; clear on re-login.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: service urls signed with token

items.title: IoT cloud headers (not HMAC-signed)
items.facts: Authorization: 'ut|<token>', app-cid: 'app:TP-Link_Tapo_Android:<terminalUUID>', x-app-name, x-app-version, x-term-id, x-ospf 'Android 14', x-net-type 'wifi', x-strict '0', x-locale (xx_YY), User-Agent, Accept json; POST adds 'Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8'. No Content-MD5 / X-Authorization.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: iot headers and no x-authorization

items.title: IoT thing list: role, status, appServerUrlV2, localAccessToken
items.facts: GET {iot}/v2/things?page=N&pageSize=100&deviceTypes=SMART.IPCAMERA,SMART.TAPODOORBELL,SMART.TAPOHUB&includePcDevice=false&includeKasaShareDevices=true&includeMatterDevice=false&includeExternalVendorDeviceInfo=true with IoT headers. Reply {code:0, data:[thing...], total}. Per thing: thingName|deviceId (key), status (int; ==1 online), role (int, 0 owner), shareType (string), appServerUrlV2|appServerUrl (thing URL for services-sync, strip /), deviceType, model, localAccessToken (non-empty string = LAT mode). Index both thingName and deviceId. Stop when items empty, seen>=total, or (no total and len<100). HTTP 401 or code in {-20651,-20652,-20675} -> token error -> one re-login (reset cached IoT URL). Skip malformed entries; never log tokens.
tests: test/unit/iot_things_test.dart: missing null empty token left out

items.title: Online state rule
items.facts: online = IoT thing status == 1 (bool from int, bools rejected) OR camera answered TDP on the LAN. Device-list v2 'status' is unreliable. If the thing list fetch fails keep the previous online map; if no thing record, fall back to device list status != 0.
tests: test/unit/camera_state_test.dart: online from thing status or lan

items.title: Terminal UUID
items.facts: 32 uppercase hex chars (UUID without dashes), generated once and persisted; sent as terminalUUID / termID / x-term-id. Baseline _newClient already does this; move it to secure store with the token. Logout clears it in baseline (kTerminal removed): keep it stable across sign-out/in to avoid MFA prompts.
tests: test/unit/app_state_test.dart: terminal uuid format and stability

items.title: Alias decoding
items.facts: alias from device list is plain UTF-8 normally. Treat as Base64 ONLY when len%4==0, len>=4, strict base64 decodes to printable UTF-8 and re-encodes to the same string; else keep verbatim. Fall back to deviceName, then model.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: decode alias plain vs base64

items.title: TDP v2 probe packet (UDP 20002 and 20004)
items.facts: Packet = 16-byte big-endian header + compact JSON. Header: u8 version=2, u8 reserved=0, u16 opcode=1, u16 payloadLen, u8 flags (0x11 broadcast request = 0x10|0x01; 0x21 unicast), u8 ret=0, u32 serial (random < 2^28), u32 CRC32. CRC32 (IEEE/zlib) computed over the whole packet with bytes 12..15 set to 0x5A6B7C8D, result written big-endian at 12. Payload {"params":{"rsa_key":"<PEM SubjectPublicKeyInfo RSA-2048>"}} compact. One RSA key pair per process, reused. Send 3 probes 0.3 s apart to 255.255.255.255 and each interface directed broadcast, ports 20002 and 20004; collect replies for ~3 s from a socket bound to an ephemeral port with SO_BROADCAST.
tests: test/unit/tdp_discovery_test.dart: probe golden vector byte exact
test/unit/tdp_discovery_test.dart: serial out of range rejected

items.title: TDP reply parsing and validation
items.facts: Replies may be concatenated: loop while >=16 bytes remain; len==0 or truncated -> stop; CRC mismatch (recompute with seed in slot) -> stop (framing unreliable); skip packet if version!=2, ret not in {0,1} or serial != probe serial. Payload JSON {error_code:0, result:{ip, mac, device_type, device_model, device_id (MD5 upper hex, may be present next to encrypt_info), encrypt_type:[..], tpap:{pake:[..],user_hash_type?,port?}, encrypt_info:{key,data}}}. error_code != 0 or missing result -> ignore. ip from result.ip (valid IPv4) else sender address. Identity: md5 = MD5(decrypted device_id) if encrypt_info decrypts, else top-level device_id lowercased if 32-hex, else ''. http_port from decrypted http_port, 0 or invalid -> null (default 443). Dedupe by normalised MAC (first wins). Never throw on hostile datagrams.
tests: test/unit/tdp_discovery_test.dart: encrypted reply yields md5 and port
test/unit/tdp_discovery_test.dart: serial and version mismatch ignored

items.title: encrypt_info decryption (RSA-OAEP-SHA1 + AES-128-CBC)
items.facts: encrypt_info = {sym_schm:'AES', key:b64, data:b64}. key_iv = RSA-OAEP(MGF1-SHA1, hash SHA1, no label) decrypt of b64(key); need >=32 bytes: AES key = key_iv[0:16], CBC IV = key_iv[16:32]. data = b64 -> AES-128-CBC -> PKCS7 unpad -> UTF-8 JSON {device_id (40-hex full id), http_port, connect_ssid, connect_type, owner}. Any failure returns {} (identity then falls back to top-level md5). Dart needs an RSA lib (pointycastle) for keygen 2048 + OAEP-SHA1; key generation on a TV CPU can take seconds: generate once, off the UI isolate, cache in memory (PEM must be SPKI with 64-char lines + trailing LF per the app, Windows uses cryptography default PEM).
tests: test/unit/tdp_discovery_test.dart: decrypt_info roundtrip with generated key
test/unit/tdp_discovery_test.dart: wrong key falls back to top level md5

items.title: Broadcast target list
items.facts: Targets = 255.255.255.255 plus the directed broadcast of every non-loopback, non-link-local IPv4 interface with prefix < 31, each on ports 20002 and 20004. Dart: enumerate with NetworkInterface.list(type: IPv4) (no netmask in dart:io: get prefix via Kotlin ConnectivityManager/LinkProperties over a MethodChannel, else assume /24). Replies are unicast to the probe socket; if an Android TV box drops them, hold a WifiManager.MulticastLock via MethodChannel.

items.title: Cloud <-> LAN matching
items.facts: normalise_mac: strip [\s:.-], uppercase, must be 12 hex else '' ; output AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF. device_id_md5 = lowercase MD5 hex of the UTF-8 deviceId. Pass 1: map LAN devices by lowercased md5 (first wins) and assign to cloud devices by md5(deviceId). Pass 2: for unmatched cloud devices, match by normalised MAC among unused LAN devices. Each LAN device is used at most once; an md5 match always beats a MAC match; unmatched cloud devices are absent. Matched cameras get host=ip, https_port=http_port||443, lan_found=true, control_protocol 'tpap' when tpap_requested(raw.tpap, raw.encrypt_type).
tests: test/unit/lan_matcher_test.dart: md5 wins and lan used once

items.title: TPAP selection hint from TDP
items.facts: tpap_requested = tpap.pake non-empty OR '4' in encrypt_type list (str/int or list). Hint stored as control_protocol='tpap' and then login skips the v3 probe. Also user_hash_type==1 in tpap hints selects SHA256U('admin') as the register user name. Even without a hint, a -40211 reply to v3 step 1 switches to TPAP (confirmed; no fallback after that).

items.title: Secure login (encrypt_type 3) hash primitives
items.facts: SHA256U = SHA-256 over UTF-8, UPPERCASE hex. MD5U = MD5 UPPERCASE hex. cnonce = 8 random bytes as 16 UPPERCASE hex chars. first_hash = SHA256U(cnonce + SHA256U(password) + nonce). expected device_confirm = first_hash + nonce + cnonce (camera proves it knows the password; compare constant-time against result.data.device_confirm BEFORE sending digest, no login attempt is spent). digest_passwd = SHA256U(SHA256U(password) + cnonce + nonce) + cnonce + nonce. In LAT mode the secret is the raw LAT instead of the password: try [LAT, password] against device_confirm and use whichever verifies.
tests: test/unit/local_crypto_test.dart: verify device confirm constant time

items.title: Secure session keys, cipher, envelope and tag
items.facts: lsk = SHA256('lsk'+cnonce+nonce+first_hash)[0:16], ivb = SHA256('ivb'+cnonce+nonce+first_hash)[0:16] (raw bytes of the digest, first 16). Cipher AES-128-CBC/PKCS7 with fixed lsk/ivb; base64 standard padded, no newlines; decrypt validates base64, positive multiple of 16, padding, UTF-8 (errors are protocol errors => session invalid). Request = compact JSON (no spaces, no ASCII escaping, no \/ escaping) of inner dict, encrypted, wrapped as {"method":"securePassthrough","params":{"request":"<b64>"}} (exact string is hashed for the tag). Headers per request: seq=<n>, tapo_tag=SHA256U(SHA256U(SHA256U(password)+cnonce) + outerBody + str(seq)). seq starts at login start_seq and increments for EVERY attempt (consumed even if the request fails). POST /stok=<stok>/ds. Reply {error_code, result:{response:<b64>}} -> decrypt -> JSON.
tests: test/unit/local_crypto_test.dart: decrypt garbage is protocol error

items.title: Local login state machine (TPAP / secure v3 / legacy MD5)
items.facts: POST / with {"method":"login","params":{...}} (compact JSON). Step 1 (always): {cnonce, encrypt_type:'3', username:'admin'}. error_code -40211 -> TPAP (confirmed, no fallback). -40413 with result.data {nonce, device_confirm} -> secure v3 step 2 {cnonce, encrypt_type:'3', username, digest_passwd}; step 2 code!=0 -> auth error; result.stok + result.start_seq required. Anything else -> legacy {hashed:true, password:MD5U(password), username:'admin'}; result.stok; requests are then plain JSON on /stok=<stok>/ds without tag. If TDP hinted TPAP, skip step 1. If device_confirm matches neither LAT nor password: auth error WITHOUT sending digest. -40404/-40408 -> locked (result.data.sec_left seconds). HTTP 401 -> auth error, other non-200 -> protocol error. Session invalid on top-level or per-item -40401, securePassthrough -40210, HTTP 401: re-login once and retry once; second failure raises.
tests: test/unit/camera_control_client_test.dart: persistent expiry gives up after one retry

items.title: Local HTTPS transport: headers, TOFU pin, keep-alive
items.facts: HTTPS to host:https_port (443 or TDP http_port). Headers: Accept application/json, User-Agent 'Tapo CameraClient Android', requestByApp 'true', Referer 'https://host:port', Content-Type 'application/json; charset=UTF-8' (TPAP /ds: application/octet-stream both ways), keep-alive. Camera certs are self-signed: no chain validation (badCertificateCallback) but pin sha256(DER) of the leaf on first contact per host:port (TOFU) and fail with CertificateMismatch on change; persist pins. Reuse one connection; on stale socket (reset/EOF) reconnect and resend once; timeouts are NOT retried (10 s). Serialise requests per camera (one lock) so seq cannot desync.

items.title: Auth circuit breaker and lockout rules
items.facts: After a TapoAuthError (wrong password / device_confirm mismatch / TPAP refusal) further logins on that client fail fast with the same error for 120 s (auth_retry_after) or until reset_auth_backoff() (user re-entered password OR the camera's LAT changed => rebuild client). Lockout (-40404/-40408) is NOT breakered here: raised immediately with sec_left. TPAP: at most 2 pake_share attempts per login (MAX_ATTEMPTS=2); never loop credential variants; background callers (status poll, events) must not retry a failed login. Shared cameras (role!=0) never log in locally. Success clears the breaker.
tests: test/unit/camera_control_client_test.dart: wrong password fails fast without new login attempts
test/unit/camera_control_client_test.dart: breaker expires after 120 s and reset allows retry

items.title: TPAP pake_register request/reply
items.facts: POST / {method:'login', params:{sub_method:'pake_register', username, user_random:b64(32 random bytes), cipher_suites:[1], encryption:['aes_128_ccm'], passcode_type:'userpw'}}. username = md5hex('admin') = 21232f297a57a5a743894a0e4a801fc3 (lowercase), or SHA256U('admin') when TDP user_hash_type==1; on -40209 retry once with literal 'admin' (remember choice). Reply result: dev_random(b64), dev_salt(b64), dev_share(b64 SEC1 point), iterations (default 10000, valid 1..10_000_000), cipher_suites (must be 1), encryption (default aes_128_ccm; other -> unsupported), extra_crypt (optional). -40413 with encrypt_type ['3'] -> not TPAP (fall back to v3 unless the camera itself demanded TPAP). Lock codes -40404/-40408 stop at once.
tests: test/unit/tpap_test.dart: register request matches the app
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: needs v3 raises not supported

items.title: SPAKE2+ (RFC 9383) prover on P-256 with SHA-256
items.facts: Suite SPAKE2+-P256-SHA256-HKDF-SHA256-HMAC-SHA256 (cipher_suites 1). w0,w1 = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(passcode UTF-8, dev_salt, iterations, 80 bytes): w0 = int(dk[0:40]) mod n, w1 = int(dk[40:80]) mod n. Context = SHA256('PAKE V1' || user_random || dev_random). Prover: x random in [1,n-1]; shareP = x*G + w0*M (uncompressed SEC1 65 B). Verifier share Y (dev_share) must be on the curve. z = x*(Y - w0*N), v = w1*(Y - w0*N). Transcript TT = for each of [context, idProver(empty), idVerifier(empty), M(uncomp), N(uncomp), shareP, shareV, Z, V] u64-LE length || bytes, then u64-LE 32 || w0(32 B big-endian). K_main = SHA256(TT). K_confirm = HKDF-SHA256(K_main, salt none, info 'ConfirmationKeys', 64): K_confirmP=first 32, K_confirmV=last 32. confirmP = HMAC-SHA256(K_confirmP, shareV) (sent as user_confirm); confirmV = HMAC-SHA256(K_confirmV, shareP) (must equal dev_confirm, constant-time compare; mismatch => auth error without retry). K_shared = HKDF-SHA256(K_main, none, 'SharedKey', 32). M = 02886e2f97ace46e55ba9dd7242579f2993b64e16ef3dcab95afd497333d8fa12f, N = 03d8bbd6c639c62937b04d997f38c3770719c629d7014d49a24b4f98baa1292b49 (compressed). Dart: implement with pointycastle ECCurve_secp256r1 (or BigInt affine like Windows); needs HKDF/HMAC/PBKDF2 (package:crypto has HMAC; PBKDF2 with 10k+ iterations of 80 bytes must run in an isolate).
tests: test/unit/tpap_test.dart: derive w0 w1 pbkdf2 80 bytes mod n
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: tpap context is sha256 of tag and randoms
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: points m n round trip
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: off curve peer share rejected

input.note: NOTE: the Windows test passes id_prover=client, id_verifier=server; the real camera flow uses EMPTY ids. Test both.

items.title: Passcode shaping by register extra_crypt
items.facts: passcode starts as md5hex(password) or SHA256U(password) (or SHA256U(LAT)); extra_crypt {type, params} reshapes it. type (case-insens.) 'password_shadow': passwd_id 1 -> md5-crypt($1$ prefix; unchanged if prefix not $1$), 2 -> sha1 hex lowercase, 3 -> unchanged (needs a user name, cameras send none), 5 -> sha256-crypt (Drepper; prefix '$5$[rounds=N$]salt$', salt<=16 chars, default 5000 rounds, rounds clamped 1000..999999999). 'password_authkey': out[i]=dictionary[(cred[i] xor tmpkey[i]) % len(dictionary)] over max(len), pad missing with 187. 'password_sha_with_salt': sha256hex((sha_name==0?'admin':'user') + utf8(b64decode(sha_salt)) + cred). Missing/malformed/unknown -> unchanged. C200 fw 1.5.7 uses shadow id 5 with SHA256U first.
tests: test/unit/tpap_crypt_test.dart: md5 crypt vector and prefix check

items.title: TPAP pake_share and candidate order (bounded attempts)
items.facts: pake_share: {sub_method:'pake_share', user_share:b64(shareP), user_confirm:b64(confirmP)}. Reply result: dev_confirm(b64, must equal confirmV), stok (required), start_seq (required int), expired (seconds, optional -> session expiry; re-login when reached). Candidate order per login (max 2 shares, each preceded by a FRESH pake_register): [LAT variant if a LAT exists] then password variants ['sha256','md5'] when register carried extra_crypt else ['md5','sha256']; no password => LAT only. After a success only the known-good variant is used, a refusal of it is retried once after 2 s (C200 refuses first share after a session ended). Two refusals => TapoAuthError (message mentions LAT use but never the token) and breaker. Empty password AND no LAT => error before any request. All secrets excluded from toString/logs.
tests: test/unit/tpap_test.dart: wrong password raises auth error after exactly two attempts
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: dev confirm mismatch is auth error without retry
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: empty password never reaches the camera

test/unit/tpap_test.dart: lat only without password logs in

items.title: TPAP /ds channel: AES-128-CCM framing
items.facts: key = HKDF-SHA256(ikm=K_shared, salt='tp-kdf-salt-aes128-key', info='tp-kdf-info-aes128-key', L=32)[0:16]; nonceBase = HKDF-SHA256(K_shared, salt 'tp-kdf-salt-aes128-iv', info 'tp-kdf-info-aes128-iv', L=32)[0:12]. nonce(seq) = nonceBase[0:8] || u32_be(seq). AES-CCM tag 16 B, no AAD. Request body = u32_be(seq) || ciphertext || tag, POST /stok=<stok>/ds, Content-Type and Accept application/octet-stream; first seq = start_seq, every attempt burns a seq. Reply body: first 4 bytes seq (reply's own) then ct||tag; nonce from that seq. Plaintext JSON replies (starts with '{' and parses with error_code) mean refusal: -40401,-40418,-40420,-40421,-2402 => session invalid (re-login once); other codes => device error and drop session. HTTP 401 => session invalid; other non-200 => protocol error. Decrypt failure => session invalid. Only 'aes_128_ccm' supported (pointycastle CCMBlockCipher/AESEngine or package:cryptography AesCcm).
tests: test/unit/tpap_test.dart: cipher golden vector and framing
test/unit/tpap_test.dart: nonce depends on seq and tamper detected

items.title: Local access token (LAT) mode
items.facts: Some cameras reject the TP-Link ID password (-40401 on login) and accept only the cloud-issued localAccessToken from the IoT thing list. TPAP passcode = SHA256U(LAT) (UPPERCASE hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 token) offered FIRST, then the password variants (within the 2-share cap). Secure v3: use raw LAT as the secret when device_confirm proves it (see local.v3_hashes). Legacy MD5 login always uses the password. :8800 media Digest secret is SHA256U(LAT) in encrypt_type 3 mode. LAT is refreshed on every sign-in/refresh: removed when the cloud returns none, kept when the fetch FAILS; a changed LAT rebuilds the control client (fresh breaker) and restarts the stream. Store per camera in secure storage. Never log or repr the token.
tests: test/unit/tpap_test.dart: lat passcode is sha256 upper of token
test/unit/camera_control_client_test.dart: v3 on password with lat given
test/unit/app_state_test.dart: refresh rotates and removes lat
test/unit/app_state_test.dart: fetch failure keeps cached lat

items.title: Reference: :8800 Digest secret and HKDF stream keys (media lane owns the code)
items.facts: Digest secret = SHA256U(secret) when encrypt_type '3' else MD5U(secret); secret = LAT in LAT mode else password. Key-Exchange header with algorithm HKDF: ikm = nonce + ':' + transformedSecret (UTF-8), salt = Key-Exchange 'salt' as UTF-8, HKDF-SHA256 L=16, info 'stream_hkdf_aes_key' / 'stream_hkdf_hmac_key'; IV = per-part X-Nonce; X-Data-Hmac = b64 HMAC-SHA256(ciphertext). Listed here so the control lane hands the right secret to the media lane.
tests: test/unit/local_media_test.dart: hkdf keys match reference derivation

vectors.note: test asserts the formula; hex computed offline by the audit

items.title: multipleRequest envelope and item normalisation
items.facts: Every command is {method, params}; batches are {"method":"multipleRequest","params":{"requests":[...]}} (order kept; empty list allowed locally, cloud sends nothing for an empty batch). Reply result.responses[] items {method, result:{...}, error_code:int|numeric string}; item normalised to {method:String?, result:Map (non-map -> {}), error_code:int}. Top-level error_code!=0 => device error 'multipleRequest'. Item error_code != 0 => device error(code, method). Numbers are string-encoded by the camera: accept int or integer string; reject bool. Parsers must throw a protocol error (never cast errors) on unusable data.
tests: test/unit/camera_dtos_test.dart: multiple request preserves order and empty
test/unit/camera_dtos_test.dart: normalize item error code string
test/unit/camera_dtos_test.dart: parsers never throw non protocol errors

items.title: getDeviceInfo / getAppComponentList
items.facts: getDeviceInfo params {device_info:{name:['basic_info']}}; parse result.device_info.basic_info: device_model (required non-empty), device_alias, sw_version, hw_version, mac, dev_id, keep raw map. getAppComponentList params {app_component:{name:['app_component_list']}}; result.app_component.app_component_list[] {name, version(int|string)} -> map name->int. Component list gates features per model (e.g. ptz/lens_mask/siren): a getter the camera does not support answers non-zero item error_code and the UI shows the default.

test/unit/camera_dtos_test.dart: parse component list string versions

items.title: Privacy mode (lens mask)
items.facts: get: {method:'getLensMaskConfig', params:{lens_mask:{name:['lens_mask_info']}}}; parse result.lens_mask.lens_mask_info.enabled 'on'|'off' (anything else = protocol error). set: {method:'setLensMaskConfig', params:{lens_mask:{lens_mask_info:{enabled:'on'|'off'}}}}. Baseline TV currently uses privacy through cloud passthrough already (getPrivacyMode/setPrivacyMode): reuse DTO builders so LAN and cloud share the payload. Cloud error -64324 means privacy is on (PTZ blocked).

items.title: PTZ: motorMove, singalMove (sic), stopMove, presets
items.facts: move: {method:'motorMove', params:{motor:{move:{x_coord:'<int as string>', y_coord:'<int as string>'}}}} (signed integer strings, dx>0 = pan right). step: {method:'singalMove' (typo is the real name), params:{motor:{movestep:{direction:'0'|'90'|'180'|'270'}}}}, other directions rejected. stop: {method:'stopMove', params:{motor:{stop:'null'}}} (string 'null'). presets: getPresetConfig {preset:{name:['preset']}} -> parallel arrays result.preset.preset {id,name,position_pan,position_tilt,read_only}; goto {method:'motorMoveToPreset', params:{preset:{goto_preset:{id:'<str>'}}}}; add {method:'addMotorPostion' (sic), params:{preset:{set_preset:{name, save_ptz:'1'}}}}; delete {method:'deletePreset', params:{preset:{remove_preset:{id:['<str>']}}}}. PTZ errors: -64303 motor busy, -64304 limit reached, -64324 privacy on, -64336 privacy zone.
tests: test/unit/camera_dtos_test.dart: motor move coords are signed int strings
test/unit/camera_dtos_test.dart: goto and delete preset ids are strings

items.title: Night vision / day-night (IR) mode
items.facts: Windows app uses the day/night config: get {method:'getDayNightModeConfig', params:{image:{name:'common'}}} (note name is a STRING here), parse result.image.common.inf_type in {'auto','on','off'}; set {method:'setDayNightModeConfig', params:{image:{common:{inf_type:'auto'|'on'|'off'}}}}. The spec also lists newer getNightVisionModeConfig/setNightVisionModeConfig (enum night_vision_mode) for models that expose a different component: pick by component list. DayNightMode values: auto, on, off.

items.title: Status LED, manual siren/alarm, motion detection
items.facts: LED get {getLedStatus {led:{name:['config']}}} -> result.led.config.enabled on/off; set {setLedStatus {led:{config:{enabled}}}}. Siren/alarm: {method:'doManualAlarm', params:{msg_alarm:{manual_alarm:{action:'start'|'stop'}}}} (the Windows app keeps its own alarm flag; no getter). Motion: get {getDetectionConfig {motion_detection:{name:['motion_det'],table:['region_info']}}} -> result.motion_detection.motion_det {enabled on/off, digital_sensitivity int|string optional}; set {setDetectionConfig {motion_detection:{motion_det:{enabled, digital_sensitivity?:'20'|'60'|'80'}}}} (other levels rejected). Reboot {rebootDevice {system:{reboot:{}}}} is out of scope for the TV (never move/reboot real cameras in tests).

items.title: Rename (setDeviceAlias) and name rules
items.facts: Request {method:'setDeviceAlias', params:{system:{sys:{dev_alias:<name>}}}}; sent through the SAME route as other commands (LAN client or cloud passthrough); no separate cloud call, the cloud picks the alias up from the camera. Validation before sending: NFC-normalise, trim, non-empty, no control chars (category Cc), <= 32 UTF-8 BYTES (not chars). Camera refusal -63103 (alias format) or -40210 => message 'refused' with code. Only owned cloud cameras (role==0) rename on the camera; shared cameras (role!=0) and manual cameras keep a local display name. After a rename keep pending_name (wins over cloud alias until the cloud alias matches or 24 h). Dart: NFC needs a package (e.g. unorm_dart) or restrict to a no-op check.

items.title: Clip search request shapes (SD playback lane)
items.facts: searchDateWithVideo {playback:{search_year_utility:{channel:[0], start_date:'yyyyMMdd', end_date}}}; searchVideoWithUTC {playback:{search_video_with_utc:{id:1 | player_id:<32hex>, channel:0, start_time, end_time, start_index, end_index}}} page size 100, repeat while result.playback.to_be_continued != 0. Error -71103 => retry the page ONCE with the other form (id <-> player_id) and remember the working form. Out of the live-view MVP, listed for the playback lane.

items.title: Cloud passthrough request (services-sync)
items.facts: POST {thing.appServerUrlV2 || appServerUrl}/v1/things/{thingName percent-encoded as ONE path segment}/services-sync with IoT headers (not signed), body {"serviceId":"passthrough","inputParams":{"requestData":{"method":"multipleRequest","params":{"requests":[...]}}}}. 30 s timeout. url must be http(s) without query/fragment; refuse http when the account API is https. Baseline posts to a discovered IoT server 'v2' (fallback v1) instead of the per-thing URL and always /v2: Windows evidence uses /v1 with the thing's own regional URL; keep the thing URL as primary (open question on v2).

items.title: Cloud passthrough reply and error mapping
items.facts: Reply {outputParams:{responseData:{error_code, result:{responses:[...]}}}}; some paths put responseData directly in outputParams, or nest under result.outputParams: accept all. cloud code = first non-zero of code|errorCode|error_code. HTTP 401 or code in {-20651,-20652,-20675} => refresh token once (single-flight across concurrent callers; skip if token already changed) and retry once, then 'session expired'. -20571 => 'Camera is offline'; -20002, 12202 or HTTP 408 => 'Camera did not respond'; HTTP 429 => 'cloud busy'; -20580 => not linked to this account; other => TP-Link cloud error <code>. responseData.error_code!=0 => device error ('multipleRequest') except offline/timeout codes. responses[] normalised like the LAN items (per-item errors stay in the items).

items.title: Per-camera routing: local, cloud passthrough, relay
items.facts: cloud_routed = camera is a cloud camera AND (role != 0 OR not (lan_found AND host non-empty)). Cloud-routed: control via passthrough, live via relay (cloudType 2), playback via relay VOD, motion events polled at most every 30 s. Else (owner, found on LAN): local HTTPS :443 control, :8800 live/playback. No signed-in cloud for a remote camera => error NETWORK_ONLY; offline cloud camera => 'Camera is offline'; shared without cloud => SHARED_CLOUD_ONLY. Optional camera account => ONVIF :2020 / RTSP :554 (not for MVP). Re-run TDP + thing list on refresh; a camera that moves LAN<->remote switches route on next call (rebuild clients).

items.title: Shared-camera rule (never log in locally)
items.facts: A camera with thing role != 0 (shared to this account) is ALWAYS cloud-routed even when found on the LAN: the user's own TP-Link ID password is not that camera's credential and every local attempt burns lockout counters. role comes from the IoT thing record (fallback: device-list role), share_type string kept. Controls for shared cameras go through passthrough with the user's own token (works); rename is local-only display name; which commands a shared user may send is unverified on hardware.

items.title: Batched status read (cloud) and alarm polling
items.facts: Remote status = ONE passthrough multipleRequest with [getLensMaskConfig, getDayNightModeConfig, getLedStatus, getDetectionConfig]; an item with non-zero error_code (unsupported model) yields its default (false / auto). LAN status reads each separately with the same defaults. Remote/shared cameras: poll getLastAlarmInfo at most every 30 s (each poll is a cloud call).
tests: test/unit/camera_router_test.dart: remote status single call with defaults

items.title: Secure storage and what persists
items.facts: Windows (DPAPI vault): TP-Link ID email+password ONLY when 'keep me signed in'; per-camera local access token (user 'admin'); settings: account (non-secret: email, nickname, accountId, region_url), terminal_uuid, TLS pins {host:port: sha256 DER}. Cloud token lives in memory only. Android TV: flutter_secure_storage (Keystore-backed EncryptedSharedPreferences) for token, password (if kept), LATs, terminal uuid; pins and non-secret settings may stay in shared_preferences. Baseline stores the session token + refreshToken in plain SharedPreferences (tapo_cloud/app_state.dart:252): migrate and wipe the old key. Sign-out deletes token, password, LATs, pins of cloud cameras; keep terminal uuid. Secrets never in logs/toString/crash reports; adb backup disabled for the secure store.
tests: test/unit/secure_store_test.dart: sign out wipes token password lat
test/unit/secure_store_test.dart: legacy shared_preferences session migrated and removed

items.title: Gaps of the TV baseline versus the Windows protocol
items.facts: tapo_cloud.dart/app_state.dart today: (1) bootstrap n-wap-gw.tplinkcloud.com and key appServerUrl instead of getAccountStatusAndUrl -> appServerUrlV2; (2) no common query params (appName, appVer, netType, termID, ospf, brand, locale); (3) appVersion 3.21.114 vs 3.22.806 used on real hardware; (4) device list requests only SMART.IPCAMERA (no doorbell); (5) IoT server id 'nbu.iot-app-server.app' (Windows: '-v2') and services-sync built from the discovered IoT server, not the thing's appServerUrlV2; (6) no IoT thing list: no role, status or localAccessToken; (7) no captchaLogin / password refresh, token in plain SharedPreferences; (8) no local control at all (TDP, v3, TPAP, LAT, pins); (9) only privacy and PTZ move are implemented; (10) every control goes through the cloud. User-Agent okhttp/3.12.13 vs app UA for IoT calls.
tests: test/unit/tapo_cloud_test.dart: regression of the above once fixed

decisions: Tier legend: 1 = pure Dart unit (crypto, DTOs, parsers, golden vectors, no I/O); 2 = protocol client against a fake transport/server in test; 3 = app-state/routing/storage with fakes; 4 = Android native (Kotlin) or UI. Priority P0 = needed for the local+cloud live-view MVP (sign-in -> list -> local or relay live view -> privacy/PTZ).

Windows behaviour is the reference where it differs from the TV baseline (appServerUrlV2, getAccountStatusAndUrl, -v2 IoT service id, common query params, thing-list roles). Baseline Topo code is kept only where it equals Windows.

Local control stack order of implementation: local_crypto (v3) -> camera_transport (TOFU pin) -> camera_control_client (login state machine + breaker) -> tpap (SPAKE2+ + CCM) -> LAT wiring. Live view on current C200-class firmware needs TPAP, so tpap is P0, not optional.

The TP-Link ID password cannot be dropped: the camera's local passcode (v3 secret, TPAP md5/sha256 candidates) and captchaLogin refresh need it. PORTING_BRIEF says 'never store the cloud password' -> proposal: store it only in Keystore-backed flutter_secure_storage, only after an explicit 'Keep me signed in' choice (default on for TV remote use, easy wipe on sign-out); LAT-only cameras and cloud-routed cameras work without it after sign-in (token + LAT). Needs the owner's approval.

SPAKE2+ and RSA-OAEP need a Dart crypto library (pointycastle or package:cryptography) because package:crypto has only hashes/HMAC. Run PBKDF2 (>=10k iterations x 80 B), RSA-2048 keygen and P-256 scalar mults in a background isolate; port the Windows BigInt affine arithmetic only as a fallback. Validate with the RFC 9383 vector before wiring to a camera.

Never test against real cameras. All local flows are tested against a Dart fake camera (port of tests/fixtures/mock_tapo_server: dispatcher, tpap_server, secure v3, legacy) and a fake cloud (port of tests/fixtures/mock_cloud.py). Golden vectors in this file are the byte-level gate.

Cloud-routed cameras (remote or shared) use the same DTO builders and the same ControlApi interface as LAN, with RemoteControlClient/CloudPassthrough as the transport (same pattern as Windows ControlApi).
Online state: IoT thing status==1 OR found by TDP; role from the thing record decides shared (role != 0).

Vector provenance: most vectors are copied from specs or tests in the Windows repo. Entries whose note says 'computed offline by the audit' were derived with hashlib/hmac/cryptography from the Windows test INPUTS (the tests assert the formula, not a literal); re-verify them against the Windows implementation when writing the Dart test.

TDP discovery uses dart:io RawDatagramSocket (broadcast) plus a MethodChannel for interface netmasks and a WifiManager MulticastLock when needed; no Kotlin crypto is required, all crypto stays in Dart.
Passwords, tokens, LATs, stok, keys: never in logs, toString, exceptions or test snapshots. Fake values only (test_password, 192.168.1.x).
open_questions: Does flutter_secure_storage (Keystore) satisfy the 'never store the cloud password' rule when the user opts in? Without the password captchaLogin refresh, v3/TPAP password variants and md5/sha256 passcodes cannot work, so only LAT/cloud-routed cameras would work after token expiry.

services-sync version: Windows uses {thing appServerUrlV2}/v1/things/{id}/services-sync (proven on owned and shared C510W); baseline tries v2 first and falls back to v1 on 404/405/501. Is /v2 ever needed? Verify with the owner before dropping the fallback.
Does a TV box receive unicast TDP replies without a MulticastLock, and can dart:io read interface netmasks? (needs a device test, no cameras needed beyond the owner's LAN).
Dart TPAP performance: PBKDF2 plus affine BigInt/pointycastle EC math on low-end TV SoCs; measure. Fallback: native Kotlin (BouncyCastle/JCA) behind a MethodChannel for SPAKE2+ only.
NFC normalisation for camera names (Vietnamese diacritics) needs a package or Kotlin java.text.Normalizer via channel.

Night vision: Windows uses getDayNightModeConfig only; the spec also has getNightVisionModeConfig for newer models. Which component name gates it (see capability.night_vision)? Not verified on hardware.
Which commands a shared user may send through passthrough is unverified (Windows AGENTS section 8); rename for shared cameras stays local.
App version/UA: baseline reports 3.21.114, Windows 3.22.806 (proven on hardware). Confirm the cloud accepts the newer version string from a TV terminalName/'Android 14' platform.

Terminal name for MFA 'trusted devices' list: Windows 'Tapo Desktop (Windows PC)', baseline 'Topo TV - Android TV'. Keep a TV-specific name; unknown whether the server validates it (spec marks it unresolved).
Session expiry for TPAP uses result.expired seconds; v3 sessions have no stated expiry: confirm -40401 handling on long-running TV live sessions (reconnect strategy shared with the media lane).

Exact Windows test line for a v3 server-side nonce/device_confirm fixture sits in tests/fixtures/mock_tapo_server/camera.py (fixed_nonce, fixed_start_seq); port that fixture rather than inventing a new one.
